title: Iryo CEO Reports Train Reconnection Delays After Signaling Failure
text: Iryo CEO Reports Train Reconnection Delays After Signaling Failure The CEO of Iryo testified in the Senate regarding persistent issues with the LZB signaling system, which frequently causes trains to stop and requires lengthy delays to reconnect. This system failure is believed to have contributed to the recent collision where an AVE train crashed into a stationary Iryo train on the same track. The CEO of Iryo reported to the Senate that his company's trains were taking 'quite a long time' to reconnect after the LZB signaling system failed. The Independent Authority for the Investigation of Railway, Maritime, and Civil Aviation Accidents (AITS) participated in the retrieval of on-board recorders alongside judicial police and railway companies. The accident occurred when an AVE train collided with an Iryo train that had stopped due to a signal failure, with the impact estimated to have occurred at speeds between 160 and 200 km\/h.This caused the front car of the AVE to become embedded in the rear car of the Iryo train, resulting in both cars overturning and sliding down the embankment. The AITS is currently in the information gathering phase, collecting data from various records and will proceed with further investigative actions in the coming weeks.
